newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex updates average crude port shipping volumes.
newsitem.headline: Pemex updates average crude port shipping volumes.

text.p: State-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) on Wednesday gave updated average shipping volumes at the nation's top three crude ports in the first nine months of 1996.

Top crude shipping port Cayo Arcas in Campeche state shipped an average 611,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil per day in the time period, compared with previous company estimates of 600,000 bpd, a Pemex spokeswoman told Reuters.
Dos Bocas in Tabasco state became the nation's second largest crude port, exporting 440,000 bpd of crude as of the first nine months in 1996, from a previous average 300,000 bpd.
Volume at Pajaritos in Veracruz state fell slightly in the time period to an average 399,000 bpd from 400,000 bpd of crude previously shipped, Pemex said.

Crude shipments at Salina Cruz port in Oaxaca state, which ships mainly to East Asia, remained an average 90,000 bpd when shipments leave the port, the spokeswoman said. Oil tankers from the port do not leave daily, however, but a few tiems a month.
